items.basis: The proposed thermal management system using a phase change material may not be effective in regulating the temperature of the battery cell during fast charging, as the study [doi:10.1109/acpee56931.2023.10135597] on fast charging method of lithium titanate battery does not provide sufficient evidence to support the use of phase change materials for thermal management in lithium-ion batteries.

The proposed system does not account for the high-temperature environment of the electric-bus depot, where the battery pack is exposed to temperatures above 40°C for extended periods, which can lead to lithium plating on the anode even with the thermal management system in place.

The study [doi:10.54337/aau681516574] on aging mechanisms in lithium-ion batteries under fast charging protocols contradicts the proposed solution, as it shows that lithium plating on the anode can occur even with real-time EIS monitoring and adjustment of charging parameters.

The proposed system is equivalent to the baseline, as the thermal management system and real-time EIS monitoring system do not provide any significant improvement over the current implementation, which does not use these features.

The integration of the real-time EIS monitoring system and the thermal management system may be technically challenging, as it requires significant changes to the existing battery management system and may not be feasible with current technology.

The testable prediction of measuring capacity fade after 3000 fast-charge cycles may be ambiguous, as the study [doi:10.5281/zenodo.19251022] on Maxwell's Electromagnetic Principles Redefinition and the Union of the Four Fundamental Forces does not provide a clear definition of capacity fade and how it should be measured.
